opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
What strikes me most is Jeremiah’s humility. He wasn’t eager to be right. He actually wished Hananiah’s prophecy were true. But he refused to reshape God’s message just to make people feel better.

That is a challenge for every Christian. We don’t follow Christ because He always promises the quickest path out of suffering. We follow Him because He is the Truth. Even when His path includes discipline, waiting, or hardship, it is ultimately the path that leads to life.

In light of recent reflections, this chapter also echoes something recognizable, our minds naturally seek immediate relief and explanations, but faith asks us to let God shape our perspective instead. Jeremiah trusted God’s word over appearances. That same trust allows us to endure seasons that don’t make sense, believing God is accomplishing something deeper than immediate comfort.
